title: Arrow-target Cartesian fibration and pullback squares
statement: Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, mapping spaces and limiting cones from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and Cartesian edges and fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $C$ be a quasicategory in a fixed universe and assume that every cospan in $C$ has a pullback, meaning a limiting cone on that cospan. Put $\operatorname{Arr}(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ and let $t=\operatorname{ev}_1:\operatorname{Arr}(C)\to C$ be target evaluation. Then $t$ is a Cartesian fibration. An edge of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$, viewed as a coherent square $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to C$, is $t$-Cartesian if and only if this square is a pullback. For $f:c'\to c$ and an object $z\to c$ of the target fiber, the Cartesian lift over $f$ with target $z\to c$ is equivalent in the fiber at $c'$ to the pullback projection $z\times_c c'\to c'$. All pullbacks here are infinity-categorical pullbacks; no terminal object, presentability, or choice of pullback objects is assumed.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.1.1.1, printed pp. 531-532 (PDF pp. 549-550); transport discussion immediately following it. Also GHN Remark 9.5. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategory theorem.

proof.text: First, $\operatorname{Arr}(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ is a quasicategory by the functor-category result. The endpoint inclusion $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is degreewise injective, so exponentiation gives an isofibration $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\{1\},C)= C$; hence $t$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories. Its fiber over $c$ is the degreewise pullback $\operatorname{Arr}(C)\times_C\{c\}$: its objects are the arrows $z\to c$, and its simplices are the coherent diagrams $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to C$ whose restriction to $\Delta^n\times\{1\}$ is constant at $c$. It is a quasicategory, since the inner horn lifting of $t$ restricts to it.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.1.1, first paragraph; Definition 2.4.1.1 and Proposition 2.4.1.8; read online 2026-10-17

proof.text: Let $f:c'\to c$ and let $v':z\to c$ be an object of the target fiber. By hypothesis choose a limiting cone on the cospan $z\to c\leftarrow c'$, presented by a coherent square with apex $P=z\times_cc'$ as in [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion]; read along the cospan direction it is an edge $e_0:v\to v'$ of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$ with $v:P\to c'$ the pullback projection and $t(e_0)=f$. To show that $e_0$ is $t$-Cartesian, by [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-criterion] it suffices that for every object $u:w\to d$ of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$ the square with top $\operatorname{Map}(u,v)\to\operatorname{Map}(u,v')$ (postcomposition with $e_0$), bottom $\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c)$ (postcomposition with $f$) and vertical maps induced by $t$ is a homotopy pullback. By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square], naturally in the second arrow and compatibly with the endpoint projections, $\operatorname{Map}(u,v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(w,P)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c')}\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c')$ and $\operatorname{Map}(u,v')\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)}\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c)$, with $t$ the projection to the second factor. Hence the square $\operatorname{Map}(u,v')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ (precomposition with $u$) is a homotopy pullback, and so is the square $\operatorname{Map}(u,v)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,P)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c')$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.1.1, pullback construction and proof; Proposition 2.4.4.3; read online 2026-10-17. Mapping-space pullback criterion: Cisinski CatLR Theorem 6.6.9 and Remark 6.6.11, as stated in lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion

proof.text: Continue with the notation and the criterion square of Step 2. Since the cone is limiting, [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion] with test object $w$ says that the square $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,P)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ is a homotopy pullback. Pasting these last two squares by [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] makes the rectangle $\operatorname{Map}(u,v)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ a homotopy pullback. This rectangle is also the composite of the criterion square with the homotopy-pullback square for $v'$, since postcomposition with $e_0$ followed by the source projection is the source projection followed by composition with $P\to z$. By the 'left iff outer' clause of [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], the criterion square is a homotopy pullback, so $e_0$ is $t$-Cartesian.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.1.1, pullback construction and proof; Proposition 2.4.4.3; read online 2026-10-17. Mapping-space pullback criterion: Cisinski CatLR Theorem 6.6.9 and Remark 6.6.11, as stated in lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion

proof.text: Conversely, let $e:(a\to b)\to(z\to c)$ be a $t$-Cartesian edge of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$, viewed as a coherent square with apex $a$ on the cospan $z\to c\leftarrow b$. Fix an object $w$ of $C$ and apply [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-criterion] to the object $1_w:w\to w$ of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$: the square $\operatorname{Map}(1_w,a\to b)\to\operatorname{Map}(1_w,z\to c)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,b)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ is a homotopy pullback. By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square], $\operatorname{Map}(1_w,z\to c)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ (precomposition with $1_w$) is a homotopy pullback, and pasting by [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] makes the rectangle $\operatorname{Map}(1_w,a\to b)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,b)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ a homotopy pullback. Precomposition with the degenerate edge $1_w$ is homotopic to the identity by the unitality of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Hence in $\operatorname{Map}(1_w,a\to b)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(w,a)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_C(w,b)}\operatorname{Map}_C(w,b)$ the projection to $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,a)$ is an equivalence: a path pullback along a map homotopic to the identity retracts onto the other factor by contracting the path. By two-out-of-three, the comparison $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,a)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)}\operatorname{Map}_C(w,b)$ of the square is an equivalence. This holds for every $w$, so [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion] says that the square is a limiting cone, a pullback. The same calculation in Steps 2–3 applies to every pullback square, with its specified coherence, so a $t$-Cartesian edge is precisely a pullback square. Every edge $f:c'\to c$ and every $z\to c$ have the Cartesian lift $e_0$ of Step 2, so by Step 1 and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], $t$ is a Cartesian fibration.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.1.1, converse characterization; Proposition 2.4.4.3; read online 2026-10-17. Mapping-space pullback criterion: Cisinski CatLR Theorem 6.6.9 and Remark 6.6.11

proof.text: Let $e:y\to v\prime$ be any $t$-Cartesian lift over $f:c\prime\to c$ with target $v\prime=(z\to c)$, and let $e_0:v\to v\prime$ be the constructed lift, where $v=(z\times_c c\prime\to c\prime)$. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-opposite-homotopy-calculus] to $t$: it remains an inner fibration after taking opposites, and reversal identifies the fiber with $F^{\mathrm{op}}$, where $F=\operatorname{Arr}(C)\times_C\{c\prime\}$. The final-horn conditions for $e,e_0$ become initial-horn conditions for $e^{\mathrm{op}},e_0^{\mathrm{op}}$, with their common source $v\prime$ and common base edge $f^{\mathrm{op}}:c\to c\prime$ [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Thus these are two cocartesian lifts for $t^{\mathrm{op}}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], they are initial objects of the same lift category $L(v\prime,f^{\mathrm{op}})$; its final clause says explicitly that forgetting the comparison triangle gives an equivalence between their targets in the fiber $F^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversing that equivalence, including its two inverse-triangle witnesses, gives an equivalence between $y$ and $v$ in $F$. This is precisely the asserted objectwise comparison with the pullback projection.
